title: Heart-failure acute decompensation
description: ESC 2023 focused update + WHO PEN-HEARTS. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedHeartFailureDecompensation. Tier 1 CRITICAL — cardiogenic shock / acute pulmonary oedema (SBP <90 OR hypoperfusion signs OR SpO2 <90 OR RR >=30 OR pink frothy sputum): sit upright, high-flow O2 to SpO2 94–98%, CPAP / NIV for pulmonary oedema with respiratory distress, IV furosemide bolus 40–80 mg (or 2.5x usual oral dose) repeated 2–4 h, IV nitrate if SBP >110 (AVOID in known RV infarct), noradrenaline 0.05–0.5 µg/kg/min for shock, dobutamine 2.5–10 µg/kg/min for contractility, urgent ECG / troponin / CXR / ABG / point-of-care echo, ICU referral. Tier 2 CRITICAL — concerning decompensation (orthopnoea / PND, bilateral basal crackles, weight gain >=2 kg/3 d, raised JVP): admit, IV furosemide, salt + fluid restriction, investigate precipitant, optimise GDMT (LVEF-banded: HFrEF four pillars including SGLT2i; HFpEF volume control + SGLT2i; potassium >=5.5 holds ACE/MRA). Tier 3 WARNING — early decompensation (mild oedema or sub-2 kg weight gain): outpatient loop-diuretic step-up by 50% for 3 days, daily weights, yellow / red zone plan, review in 3–7 days. Tier 4 INFO — no decompensation: reinforce self-management, vaccinate.

title: IMCI: measles in children under 5
description: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet 2014 + WHO Measles Treatment Recommendations 2020 + Kenya MoH EPI. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedMeasles AND ageMonths < 60. Critical for severe complicated measles: any IMCI general danger sign, corneal clouding (sight-threatening), deep / extensive mouth ulcers, severe pneumonia, severe dehydration, encephalitis (seizures or altered mental state), stridor in calm child — admit; vitamin A age-banded (50 000 IU < 6 m / 100 000 IU 6–11 m / 200 000 IU >= 12 m, today and tomorrow); tetracycline 1% eye ointment + urgent ophthalmology for corneal clouding; ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IM/IV for severe pneumonia / encephalitis; manage seizures with diazepam PR / midazolam buccal; ORS / IV fluids; respiratory isolation; immunise non-immune contacts within 72 h. Critical for measles with eye / mouth / non-severe pneumonia — outpatient bundle: vitamin A, amoxicillin DT 25 mg/kg BD x 5 d for non-severe pneumonia, tetracycline eye ointment, GV paint or salicylate gel for mouth ulcers, soft feeds. Warning for uncomplicated measles — vitamin A, paracetamol, isolate 4 days post-rash, contact tracing. Info for prodrome with Koplik spots or known contact in last 21 days — vitamin A + isolation + review at 48 h.

title: PMTCT — Prevention of mother-to-child HIV transmission
description: WHO 2021 consolidated HIV prevention / treatment guidelines + Kenya NASCOP PMTCT Algorithm 2022. Critical when HIV-positive pregnant or breastfeeding AND not on ART — start tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir (TLD) same day, baseline VL / creatinine / CD4 / HBsAg / syphilis, intensive adherence counselling, plan infant prophylaxis (dual NVP + AZT for high-risk maternal profile, NVP-only for lower risk). Critical when on ART but VL >= 1000 copies/mL — repeat VL after enhanced-adherence package (3 sessions / 4–8 weeks), drug-resistance testing where available, switch to TLD if on NNRTI-based regimen, dual infant prophylaxis 12 weeks. Critical when maternal HIV status unknown — provider-initiated HIV testing today + same-day TLD if positive; offer PrEP if negative with ongoing risk. Critical when HIV-exposed infant not yet on prophylaxis — start age-banded NVP today (15 mg birth–6 w, 20 mg 6 w–6 m), add AZT for high-risk profile, cotrimoxazole from 6 weeks. Warning when virally suppressed — continue TLD, trimester VL + 6-week post-partum VL + 6-monthly thereafter, infant NVP 6 weeks, EID PCR at 6 w / 6 m / 12 m, final antibody 18 m or 6 weeks after breastfeeding stops, exclusive-feeding counselling. Warning for HIV-negative with serodiscordant partner / ongoing exposure — offer PrEP (TDF/FTC), 3-monthly retesting.

title: Postpartum care — WHO 4-contact schedule + red flags
description: WHO 2022 recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience + Kenya MoH Postnatal Care Guidelines. WHO mandates four PNC contacts in the first 6 weeks: < 24 h, day 3 (48–72 h), day 7–14, week 6. Critical for any red flag any time in the first 6 weeks: heavy bleeding / PPH (uterine massage + oxytocin 10 IU bolus + 20 IU/L infusion + TXA 1 g IV within 3 h + balloon tamponade if atony persists), fever >= 38 (puerperal sepsis — cultures + ampicillin + gentamicin + metronidazole within 1 h), foul lochia (endometritis), postpartum severe-range hypertension >=160/110 OR severe headache / visual disturbance (postpartum pre-eclampsia / eclampsia — MgSO4 4 g IV + 10 g IM, labetalol or hydralazine), calf pain / swelling (DVT — LMWH), dyspnoea (PE / cardiac), breast abscess + systemic features (incision + drainage + antibiotics), suicidal thoughts (mental-health crisis pathway). Warning when first / day-3 / day-7–14 contact overdue. Warning for postpartum anaemia (Hb < 9 g/dL) — ferrous sulphate 200 mg TDS + folic acid 5 mg daily for >=3 months, workup malaria / hookworm / HIV. Warning for EPDS >=13 — perinatal mental-health pathway (psychological therapy first; sertraline 50–100 mg daily if moderate-severe and safe in breastfeeding). Info for routine week-6 contact — contraception, infant immunisations (DTP-HepB-Hib-1, PCV-1, OPV-1, rotavirus-1, IPV-1), cervical-cancer screen offer, EPDS.

title: Chronic kidney disease — screen, stage, manage
description: KDIGO 2024 CKD Evaluation & Management + WHO PEN HEARTS + Kenya MoH NCD Guidelines. Critical when eGFR < 30 (KDIGO G4 / G5) OR acute features (AKI, refractory hyperkalaemia K >= 6, severe metabolic acidosis HCO3 < 15) — urgent nephrology referral, avoid nephrotoxins (NSAIDs / aminoglycosides / IV contrast / herbal), renal-dose every medication (metformin contraindicated at eGFR < 30), hyperkalaemia bundle (IV calcium gluconate if ECG changes + insulin / dextrose + salbutamol nebuliser + dialysis for definitive removal). Critical for heavy proteinuria (uACR >= 300 mg/g, uPCR >= 50 mg/mmol, dipstick +++) OR rapid eGFR decline (> 5 mL/min/year) — workup HIV / HBsAg / anti-HCV / ANA / SPEP, maximally tolerated ACE inhibitor or ARB, ADD SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) when eGFR >= 20 and uACR >= 200 regardless of diabetes, BP < 130 / 80, nephrology referral for biopsy if cause unclear. Warning for KDIGO G3a / G3b (eGFR 30–59) OR A2 albuminuria (uACR 30–300) — confirm chronicity, BP < 130/80, ACE/ARB, SGLT2i for diabetic kidney disease, moderate-intensity statin, avoid nephrotoxins, vaccinate (influenza / pneumococcal / hepatitis B), annual review. Warning for high-risk patient without recent eGFR / uACR — order both today (risk markers: known hypertension, diabetes, HIV, age >= 60, family history CKD, recurrent UTI, kidney stones, long-term NSAID / herbal use).

title: Severe head injury / traumatic brain injury triage
description: NICE NG232 (2023) Head injury: assessment and early management + Brain Trauma Foundation Guidelines 4th edn + CRASH-3 trial + WHO Acute Care + Kenya MoH Acute Care. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedHeadInjury. Critical for severe TBI (GCS <= 8) OR herniation features (unilateral fixed dilated pupil, motor posturing, Cushing's triad) — RSI for airway, target SpO2 >= 94 and SBP >= 110 (single episode of hypotension or hypoxia doubles mortality), 30 degree head-up, sedate, hypertonic saline 3% 250 mL OR mannitol 1 g/kg for herniation features, tranexamic acid 1 g IV + 1 g infusion 8 h if within 3 h of injury (CRASH-3), urgent CT, neurosurgical referral, reverse any anticoagulation. Critical for moderate TBI (GCS 9–12) OR any NICE high-risk feature (focal deficit, > 1 vomit, post-traumatic seizure, suspected open / depressed / basal skull fracture, age >= 65 + LOC / amnesia, anticoagulant + LOC / amnesia, dangerous mechanism + LOC / amnesia) — urgent CT brain within 1 hour, admit for neuro-obs every 30 min for 2 h then hourly for >= 24 h or until GCS 15 for 4 h, TXA if GCS <= 12 within 3 h. Warning for mild TBI (GCS 13–15) with intermediate feature (LOC / amnesia / single vomit / persistent headache / intoxication / suspected non-accidental injury in child) — 4-hour facility neuro-observation then discharge if asymptomatic with a written head-injury warning card to a responsible adult. Info for low-risk mild TBI — discharge with the written warning card and instruction to return immediately.

title: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycaemic State (HHS) — recognition + bundle
description: JBDS-IP HHS Guideline (2022) + ADA Standards of Care 2024 + WHO PEN HEARTS. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedHhs. Diagnostic triad: hypovolaemia + plasma glucose >= 30 mmol/L + osmolality >= 320 mOsm/kg WITHOUT significant ketonaemia (< 3 mmol/L) or acidosis (pH > 7.30, HCO3 > 15 mmol/L). Critical bundle: 0.9 % NaCl 15 mL/kg over the first hour then ~1 L every 2 h, switch to 0.45 % NaCl only if osmolality does not fall despite positive balance AND corrected sodium is rising; add 5 % dextrose when glucose < 14 mmol/L; fixed-rate insulin 0.05 U/kg/h (lower than DKA) ONLY after 60 min of fluids AND glucose has stopped falling OR ketones rise; potassium 40 mmol/L when K 3.5–5.5, withhold when > 5.5 with ECG monitoring; prophylactic LMWH for very high VTE risk; investigate precipitant (infection, silent MI, stroke, missed therapy, steroid load). Severity overlay (osmolality >= 350, Na >= 160, K outside 3.5–6.0, GCS <= 12, SBP < 90 after fluids, SpO2 < 92) triggers ICU input. Mixed HHS/DKA picture (glucose >= 30 + ketones >= 3) returns a warning card recommending DKA-priority management with slow osmolality correction. Cards carry ICD-10 E14.0 / E11.0, ICD-11 5A21, SNOMED 421750000, LOINC 2345-7 + 2951-2.

title: Tuberculosis treatment regimens (DS / RR / MDR / pre-XDR / XDR)
description: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on Tuberculosis — Module 4: Treatment (2022 with 2024 update) + Kenya NTLD-P Treatment Protocol. Sentinel-gated by tbConfirmed. Critical (drug-susceptible pulmonary / extrapulmonary TB) — 2HRZE/4HR with weight-banded 4FDC tablets per WHO band (25–37 / 38–54 / 55–70 / >=71 kg), paediatric child-friendly dispersible RHZ + E for < 25 kg; CNS / bone / disseminated TB extended to 9–12 months with adjunctive prednisolone for TB meningitis / pericarditis; alternative WHO 4-month 2HPMZ/2HPM rifapentine-moxifloxacin regimen for pulmonary DS-TB >= 12 y >= 40 kg. HIV co-infection: ART within 2 weeks (CD4 < 50 or TB meningitis) or 8 weeks otherwise, rifampicin doubles dolutegravir clearance so DTG 50 mg twice daily during rifampicin + 2 weeks. Pyridoxine 25–50 mg daily to prevent isoniazid neuropathy. Pregnancy-safe regimen. Critical (rifampicin-resistant / MDR-TB) — refer to PMDT site within 48 h for WHO 6-month all-oral BPaL(M): bedaquiline + pretomanid + linezolid + moxifloxacin (drop moxifloxacin if fluoroquinolone resistance). Critical (pre-XDR / XDR) — national reference centre individualised regimen with bedaquiline + linezolid + clofazimine + cycloserine ± delamanid for 18–20 months. Monthly LFTs, full blood count (linezolid myelosuppression), ECG QTc (bedaquiline + moxifloxacin), visual acuity + colour vision (ethambutol + linezolid). Mandatory case notification within 24 h; trace household contacts; offer TPT (3HP / 6H / 1HP) to <5y + PLHIV contacts. Cards carry ICD-10 A15/A16, ICD-11 1B10/1B14, SNOMED 56717001/85729005, ATC J04AM06 (HRZE) / J04AK05 (bedaquiline) / J04AK08 (pretomanid).

title: Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)
description: WHO position paper on rabies vaccines (April 2018) + CDC ACIP rabies prevention + Kenya MoH rabies elimination strategy. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedRabiesExposure. Critical (WHO Category III: transdermal bite, scratch breaking skin, mucous-membrane / broken-skin contamination, ANY bat exposure) — (1) wound care: wash with soap and running water for >=15 min then virucidal (povidone-iodine / 70% alcohol / quaternary ammonium); (2) rabies immunoglobulin HRIG 20 IU/kg (or equine RIG 40 IU/kg) infiltrated AS MUCH AS ANATOMICALLY POSSIBLE into and around each wound with any remaining volume IM distant from the vaccine site; (3) start vaccine same day — WHO 4-dose IM Essen schedule (days 0/3/7/14–28) using purified Vero-cell vaccine, OR dose-sparing intradermal Updated Thai Red Cross (0.1 mL ID at two sites days 0/3/7/28). Critical (Category II: nibbling on uncovered skin or minor scratch without bleeding) — wound care + full vaccine course, NO RIG. Critical (re-exposure after prior full PEP / pre-exposure vaccination) — abbreviated 2-dose booster days 0+3, NO RIG. Info (Category I: touch / feed / intact-skin lick) — no PEP unless contact uncertain. Pregnancy / breastfeeding / immunocompromised state are NOT contraindications. Tetanus prophylaxis + reassure that PEP is never too late as long as symptoms have not started. Notify public-health surveillance. Cards carry ICD-10 Z20.3 / Z29.2, ICD-11 1G40, SNOMED 14168008 (rabies) / 313160007 (vaccination) / 417303002 (RIG administration), ATC J07BG01 + J06BB05.

title: Neonatal jaundice — AAP 2022 thresholds + acute bilirubin encephalopathy
description: AAP 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline Revision: Management of Hyperbilirubinaemia in the Newborn >= 35 Weeks Gestation + WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2nd edn) + Kenya MoH National Newborn Care Guidelines. Critical (acute bilirubin encephalopathy: lethargy progressing to hypertonia, retrocollis/opisthotonus, shrill cry, fever, seizures) — INTENSIVE phototherapy immediately (continuous LED panels >=30 µW/cm²/nm), prepare double-volume exchange transfusion 160 mL/kg, cross-match, NPO, monitor temperature/glucose/calcium/electrolytes, investigate cause (DAT, blood group, FBC + retics + film, G6PD, sepsis, TORCH). Critical (jaundice in the first 24 h of life — NEVER physiological) — admit, TSB + direct bilirubin, DAT + maternal antibody screen, G6PD, sepsis screen, phototherapy. Critical (TSB >= AAP exchange threshold for postnatal age + risk profile — gestational age < 38 wks OR DAT+/G6PD/ABO-Rh/sepsis/dusky pallor/poor feeding) — exchange transfusion + intensive phototherapy. Critical (TSB >= AAP phototherapy threshold) — intensive phototherapy + investigate cause if rapid rise. Warning (within 2 mg/dL of threshold OR rise > 0.2 mg/dL/h) — repeat TSB 6–12 h, optimise feeding (>=8 breastfeeds in 24 h), risk-factor review. Warning (prolonged jaundice >14 d term, >21 d preterm) — measure split bilirubin (must be < 1 mg/dL or < 20% total); conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia is biliary atresia until proven otherwise — URGENT abdominal ultrasound + Kasai window < 60 d. Cards carry ICD-10 P59/P57/P55, ICD-11 KA86/KA64, SNOMED 387731001 (neonatal jaundice) / 234468005 (severe hyperbilirubinaemia), LOINC 1975-2 + 6082-2.

title: Sickle-cell disease — vaso-occlusive crisis + complications
description: American Society of Hematology 2020 Clinical Practice Guidelines for Sickle Cell Disease (Acute & Chronic Pain) + NHLBI 2014 Evidence-Based Management of Sickle Cell Disease + Kenya MoH Sickle Cell Disease Guidelines (2019). Sentinel-gated by sickleCellDisease. Critical (life-threatening SCD emergency: acute chest syndrome [new infiltrate or SpO2 < 92], stroke / focal neurology, priapism > 4 h, splenic sequestration with falling Hb, aplastic crisis Hb <6 with low retics, sepsis with fever >=38.5, severe anaemia Hb <5) — ABC + oxygen to SpO2 >=95, isotonic IV fluids at maintenance (AVOID over-hydration — risk of ACS), morphine 0.1 mg/kg IV every 10–20 min titrated, ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg + azithromycin for ACS, exchange transfusion for stroke / severe ACS / refractory priapism, urology for priapism, urgent neurology + CT/MRI for stroke (NO tPA). Critical (vaso-occlusive pain crisis NRS >=4) — analgesia within 30 min per ASH 2020, paracetamol + ibuprofen + opioid titrated, maintenance fluids, incentive spirometry, screen for precipitants, optimise hydroxyurea (15–20 mg/kg/day titrated to MCV 100–110, ANC > 2). Warning (chronic-care gaps): not on hydroxyurea (offer at >=9 months), missing penicillin V prophylaxis <5 y, missing PCV13/PPSV23/meningococcal/Hib/influenza, no annual transcranial Doppler 2–16 y, no retinal screen >=10 y, no folic-acid 5 mg daily. Cards carry ICD-10 D57/D57.0, ICD-11 3A51, SNOMED 237364002 (SCD) / 417847000 (vaso-occlusive crisis), LOINC 67881-8 (HbS%), ATC L01XX05 (hydroxyurea).

title: Dengue / chikungunya / Zika — arboviral fever triage
description: WHO Dengue Guidelines for Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention and Control (2009 + 2024 update) + WHO Handbook for Clinical Management of Dengue (2012) + PAHO Guidelines (2022) + CDC Dengue Clinical Guidance. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedArboviralFever. Critical (severe dengue, Group C): shock features (narrow pulse pressure <=20 mmHg, SBP <90), severe organ involvement (AST/ALT >=1000, GCS <=13, creatinine >200), or clinically-significant mucosal bleeding with platelets <20 — admit HDU/ICU, isotonic crystalloid 10–20 mL/kg over 1 h titrated down to 7-5-3 mL/kg/h, colloid bolus for refractory leakage with rising Hct, transfuse packed cells for occult bleeding (falling Hct despite fluids), STRICTLY NO NSAIDs / aspirin, paracetamol 15 mg/kg every 6 h (NOT every 4 h). Critical (warning signs, Group B): abdominal pain or tenderness, persistent vomiting, clinical fluid accumulation (ascites / pleural effusion), mucosal bleeding, lethargy or restlessness, hepatomegaly >2 cm, rapid platelet fall, haematocrit rise >=20% from baseline — admit IV fluids 5–7 mL/kg/h titrated, 4-hourly observations through critical phase (days 3–7). Critical override: suspected Zika in pregnancy — refer maternal-foetal medicine for serial foetal ultrasound + RT-PCR (serum + urine within 14 d). Warning (uncomplicated, Group A): outpatient supportive care + daily review during critical phase + oral fluids + paracetamol ONLY + mosquito-net protection. Chikungunya overlay (marked polyarthralgia) and Zika overlay (rash + conjunctivitis + safe-sex counselling) included.

title: Schistosomiasis — treatment + complications + MDA eligibility
description: WHO Guideline on Control and Elimination of Human Schistosomiasis (2022) + CDC Schistosomiasis Clinical Guidance + Kenya MoH National Schistosomiasis & STH Strategic Plan. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedSchistosomiasis. Critical (complicated disease: neuroschistosomiasis with myelitis / seizures / focal signs, portal hypertension with variceal bleed, massive haematuria with shock, obstructive uropathy) — admit + specialist referral + complication-specific resuscitation + prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day for neuroschistosomiasis BEFORE praziquantel + ultrasound + MRI spine/brain where indicated. Critical (Katayama fever / acute schistosomiasis 4–8 weeks post-exposure: fever + urticaria + eosinophilia + cough + hepatosplenomegaly) — prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day x 5–7 days FIRST, defer curative praziquantel 6–12 weeks. Critical (confirmed infection: positive egg / antigen / serology) — praziquantel 40 mg/kg single oral dose with food (S. mansoni / haematobium / intercalatum / guineensis), 60 mg/kg for S. japonicum / mekongi; split 20 mg/kg twice 4–6 h apart for tolerability. Pregnancy >=14 weeks safe per WHO 2006/2022. Recheck eggs / antigen at 8–12 weeks; second course if positive (efficacy ~85%). Warning (high suspicion without confirmation) — urine microscopy + stool ova + urine CCA + serology + empirical praziquantel reasonable in endemic settings. Info (MDA eligibility): yearly praziquantel 40 mg/kg for school-age (5–14 y) per WHO MDA; WHO 2022 expands to preschool + adults in high-prevalence (>=10%) settings.

title: IMCI: ear infection in children under 5 (AOM / CSOM / mastoiditis)
description: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (2014) + WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2nd edn) + AAP Clinical Practice Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Acute Otitis Media (Lieberthal et al. 2013) + Kenya MoH IMCI. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedEarProblem + ageMonths < 60. Critical (mastoiditis: tender swelling behind the ear with outward-pushed pinna) — admit, IV ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg once daily until improved + oral step-down for total 14 days; add metronidazole if suspected intracranial extension; contrast CT or MRI of the temporal bone; urgent ENT referral for myringotomy +/- mastoidectomy if not improving 48 h. Critical (AOM: pus <14 d OR bulging tympanic membrane + ear pain): amoxicillin 80–90 mg/kg/day divided twice daily for 5–10 days (10 days if <2 y or severe); co-amoxiclav for prior amoxicillin failure; macrolide for IgE-mediated penicillin allergy; AAP watchful-waiting allowed in age >=2 unilateral without otorrhoea if family can return; paracetamol + ibuprofen for analgesia. Warning (CSOM: pus >=14 days) — dry wicking >=3 times/day + topical ciprofloxacin 0.3% drops 5 drops BD for 2 weeks (or until 3 days after dryness); AVOID aminoglycoside drops (ototoxic) and oral antibiotics; safe-water practices; ENT referral if no response in 2 weeks or cholesteatoma suspected. Info (no infection) — reassure + return triggers + PCV / influenza vaccination.

title: Neonatal sepsis / Possible Serious Bacterial Infection (PSBI)
description: WHO Managing Possible Serious Bacterial Infection in Young Infants When Referral is Not Feasible (2015 simplified regimens) + WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2nd edn 2013) + WHO Sepsis 2020 + Kenya MoH National Newborn Care Guidelines (2014). Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedNeonatalSepsis (postnatal age 0–28 days). Critical (PSBI features: unable to feed since birth or stopped feeding, convulsions, movement only when stimulated, severe chest indrawing, grunting, RR >=60, temperature >=38 OR <35.5, bulging fontanelle, neck stiffness) — first-line within 1 hour: ampicillin 50 mg/kg IV/IM every 12 h (week 1) or every 8 h (week 2+) + gentamicin 5 mg/kg IM/IV once daily (4 mg/kg if <32 weeks) for 10–14 days; suspected meningitis adds ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg (or cefotaxime in jaundiced / premature) — LP when stable; full sepsis screen (blood culture >=1 mL, FBC, CRP, glucose, urine culture, CXR if respiratory features); refer to neonatal admission within 1 hour. When referral NOT possible, WHO 2015 simplified outpatient PSBI regimen: IM gentamicin once daily for 7 days + oral amoxicillin 50 mg/kg BD for 7 days with DAILY follow-up. Warning (risk-factor screen positive in a well infant: maternal chorioamnionitis, PROM >18 h, intrapartum fever, GBS+ without IAP, prematurity <35 wks) — admit 48 h observation + sepsis screen + culture-driven decision. Info (well infant): routine PNC + WHO danger-signs counselling + cord care + vitamin K 1 mg IM + BCG / OPV at birth + exclusive breastfeeding 8–12x/24 h.

title: Heat stroke / heat-related illness
description: CDC NIOSH Heat-Related Illness clinical guidance + WHO Heat and Health technical brief + Korey-Stringer Institute Exertional Heat Stroke Consensus + NEJM 2019 Heat-Related Illnesses review. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedHeatIllness. Critical (heat stroke: rectal core temperature >=40 °C OR >=39 °C with CNS dysfunction — confusion, ataxia, seizures, coma): rapid cooling within 30 minutes is the primary survival determinant — EXERTIONAL heat stroke COLD-WATER IMMERSION (head out of water, continuous rectal-temp monitoring, target <=39 °C in 30 min; stop at 39 °C to avoid overshoot); CLASSIC heat stroke evaporative cooling (continuous fanning of wet patient + ice packs neck/axillae/groin); ABC support; IV 0.9% NaCl 20 mL/kg bolus titrated; AVOID antipyretics (paracetamol / aspirin do NOT lower hyperthermic body temperature); benzodiazepine for seizures; rhabdomyolysis bundle (target urine output 2 mL/kg/h, urinary alkalinisation if severe, recheck CK / K+ / creatinine 6-hourly); ICU admission. Critical (severe heat exhaustion with red flags: SBP <90, persistent vomiting, Na <=130 or >=150, creatinine >200, dark urine suggesting rhabdomyolysis, CK > 5x ULN) — admit + IV fluids + close monitoring + escalation to heat-stroke pathway if temperature climbs or any CNS dysfunction. Warning (heat exhaustion: heat-exposure symptoms with core temp <40 °C and no CNS dysfunction) — move to cool, oral ORS 1–1.5 L over 1 h (or IV 0.9% NaCl 1 L over 1 h in vulnerable groups), rest >=30 min, recheck temperature / pulse / orthostatic BP every 15 min. Info (heat-exposure risk) — WHO counselling (hydration ~200 mL every 20 min, work-rest cycles, light loose clothing, avoid 11 am–4 pm exertion, NEVER leave infants / pets in parked vehicles, twice-daily check on vulnerable household members during heat waves).

description: On ECG-confirmed STEMI (context.stEcgFinding = 'stemi'), determines reperfusion strategy: PCI within 120 min preferred; otherwise fibrinolysis with tenecteplase / streptokinase within 12 h of symptom onset, then transfer for PCI within 24 h. Contraindication checklist (recent bleed, stroke, surgery, BP > 180/110). Reads context.symptomOnsetMin, context.transferToPciMin, context.bleedingRisk.

title: Atrial fibrillation — CHA₂DS₂-VASc anticoagulation
description: On context.diagnoses contains atrial fibrillation, computes CHA₂DS₂-VASc + HAS-BLED, recommends DOAC (apixaban/dabigatran/rivaroxaban/edoxaban) if non-valvular and CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥ 2 (men) or ≥ 3 (women). Warfarin for valvular AF / mechanical valve. Adds dose adjustment for renal function + age + weight. Reads context.diagnoses, context.ageYears, context.sex, context.creatinineClearance.

title: VTE prophylaxis — Padua score in medical inpatients
description: Computes Padua score from context. Recommends LMWH (enoxaparin 40 mg SC OD; 20 mg if CrCl < 30) or fondaparinux if Padua ≥ 4 AND HAS-BLED < 3. Mechanical (IPC) prophylaxis if pharmacological contraindicated. Reads context.paduaItems (age ≥ 70, cancer, prior VTE, bedrest, etc.) + bleeding risk + CrCl.

codings.display: Acute embolism and thrombosis of unspecified deep veins of lower extremity

title: Upper GI bleed — Glasgow-Blatchford triage
description: Computes Glasgow-Blatchford Score from context.urea, context.hb, context.systolicBp, context.pulse, context.melaena, context.syncope. Score 0 → outpatient possible; ≥ 6 → urgent endoscopy + IV PPI 80 mg bolus then 8 mg/h + terlipressin if variceal suspected.

title: Alcohol withdrawal — CIWA-Ar protocol
description: Symptom-triggered diazepam / chlordiazepoxide based on CIWA-Ar score; thiamine 200 mg IV before glucose; folate; magnesium. Recognises delirium tremens needing ICU. Reads context.ciwaScore, context.heartRate, context.tremor, context.seizureHistory.

title: Community-acquired pneumonia — CURB-65 + antibiotic choice
description: Computes CURB-65 from context.confusion, context.urea, context.respiratoryRate, context.systolicBp, context.diastolicBp, context.ageYears. 0–1 outpatient amoxicillin; 2 ward amoxicillin + macrolide; ≥ 3 IV co-amoxiclav + macrolide / consider ICU. AWaRe-tagged choices.

title: Uncomplicated UTI — empirical therapy
description: For non-pregnant women with cystitis: nitrofurantoin 100 mg BD × 3 days (preferred where eGFR ≥ 45) OR trimethoprim 200 mg BD × 3 days (avoid if local E. coli resistance > 20 %). Pregnancy: nitrofurantoin 1st-2nd trimester only; cefalexin in 3rd. Men → 7-day course + investigate. Reads context.sex, context.pregnant, context.eGFR.

codings.display: Urinary tract infection, site not specified

title: Asthma — GINA stepwise therapy
description: On context.diagnoses contains asthma + context.gina.SABAUsePerWeek, recommends GINA-aligned step: Track 1 MART (budesonide-formoterol PRN ± low/medium maintenance). Steps up if SABA ≥ 3 days/week or night-waking. Triggers severe-asthma review if step 5. Reads context.gina, context.symptomControl.

title: Iron-deficiency anaemia — replacement pathway
description: Calculates iron deficit using Ganzoni formula or simplified table. Prefers oral ferrous sulphate 200 mg OD (alternate days dosing supported by HEPCIDIN evidence). IV ferric carboxymaltose if intolerance, malabsorption, CKD-anaemia, IBD, pregnancy ≥ 14 weeks, or Hb < 70 with symptoms. Reads context.hb, context.ferritin, context.tsat, context.weightKg, context.pregnant.

title: Hypothyroidism — levothyroxine initiation
description: On TSH > 10 mU/L OR TSH 4–10 with symptoms / pregnancy / fertility planning, recommends levothyroxine 1.6 µg/kg/day (start full dose if young + no IHD; start 25 µg if elderly / IHD). Repeat TSH at 6–8 weeks. Pregnancy: aim TSH < 2.5 mU/L; increase dose by 30 % on confirmed pregnancy. Reads context.tsh, context.freeT4, context.ageYears, context.pregnant, context.ihd.

title: HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)
description: For occupational / sexual / mother-to-child exposure within 72 h: recommends TDF + 3TC (or FTC) + DTG once daily × 28 days; alternative regimens for renal impairment. Baseline + 6-week + 3-month HIV testing. Counsels source-testing where possible. Reads context.exposureType, context.hoursSinceExposure, context.sourceHivStatus, context.eGFR.

codings.display: Contact with and (suspected) exposure to human immunodeficiency virus

title: Tumour lysis syndrome risk recognition + prophylaxis
description: Fires for oncology patients about to receive cytolytic therapy in high-risk haematological malignancy (Burkitt, ALL with WBC > 100, AML with WBC > 50, bulky high-grade lymphoma). Recommends pre-emptive hydration + hypouricaemic therapy (allopurinol / rasburicase) and electrolyte monitoring per Coiffier 2008 / ESMO. Reads context.cancerType, context.WBC, context.LDH, context.uricAcid, context.creatinine, context.phosphate, context.potassium — never patient identity.

references.label: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines on TLS

title: Neutropenic sepsis emergency — Sepsis-6 within 1 hour
description: Fires for any patient with neutrophil count < 0.5 (or < 1.0 with falling trend) AND fever ≥ 38°C single OR ≥ 37.5°C sustained 1 h. Recommends immediate broad-spectrum antibiotic (piperacillin-tazobactam OR meropenem per local policy + vancomycin if line / shock / MRSA risk), blood + line cultures, lactate, fluids, urine output. References NICE CG151. Reads context.neutrophilCount, context.temperature, context.cancerTherapyStartDays, context.suspectedFocus — never patient identity.

references.label: IDSA Clinical Practice Guideline for Antimicrobial Agents in Febrile Neutropenic Cancer Patients (2010)

title: Acute intracerebral haemorrhage — BP control + anticoagulant reversal
description: Fires for any patient with imaging-confirmed ICH. Recommends acute SBP lowering to 130–140 mmHg with IV labetalol / nicardipine (INTERACT-2 / ATACH-2 targets) and immediate reversal of any anticoagulant: warfarin → vit K + 4F-PCC; dabigatran → idarucizumab; FXa DOAC → andexanet OR 4F-PCC; heparin → protamine. Antiplatelet platelet transfusion NOT recommended unless neurosurgery imminent (PATCH). Reads context.ichDiagnosis, context.systolicMmHg, context.anticoagulant, context.gcs — never patient identity.

title: mhGAP — Self-harm / acute suicide-risk pathway
description: Fires when patient has documented suicidal ideation with plan / intent OR recent self-harm act. Recommends safety-first (do not leave alone, restrict means), medical treatment of any overdose / injury (link to antidote registry: paracetamol-nac, organophosphate-atropine, tca-sodium-bicarbonate), empathic interview, treat underlying psychiatric drivers, written safety plan, follow-up within 24–72 h, mental-health specialist referral. Reads context.suicideIdeationPresent, context.suicidePlanPresent, context.recentSelfHarmAct, context.suspectedIngestion — never patient identity.

references.label: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 — Self-harm/Suicide (SUI)

title: NSAID at ≥ 20 weeks gestation — contraindicated
description: Blocks NSAID prescribing (ibuprofen, diclofenac, naproxen, indomethacin) for pregnant patients at ≥ 20 weeks gestation due to oligohydramnios and premature ductus arteriosus closure (FDA 2020 Drug Safety Communication). Recommends paracetamol as alternative. Reads context.pregnant, context.gestationWeeks, context.medications — never patient identity.

references.label: FDA Drug Safety Communication 2020 — NSAID at ≥ 20 weeks gestation

title: Codeine and tramadol in children < 12 — contraindicated
description: Blocks codeine and tramadol prescribing in children under 12 years (and post-tonsillectomy / adenoidectomy at any age 12–18, and in children with OSA / obesity 12–18) per FDA 2017 and EMA recommendations following deaths from ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metaboliser children. Recommends paracetamol + ibuprofen first, then weight-appropriate morphine if opioid needed. Reads context.ageYears, context.recentTonsillectomy, context.obstructiveSleepApnoea, context.medications — never patient identity.

references.label: FDA Drug Safety Communication 2017 — codeine + tramadol in children

title: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir (Paxlovid) — major interaction screen
description: Fires when nirmatrelvir-ritonavir is about to be prescribed. Screens current medications for major / contraindicated interactions via ritonavir CYP3A4 + P-gp inhibition: simvastatin, lovastatin (contraindicated), amiodarone, ergot alkaloids, rivaroxaban / apixaban, sildenafil for PAH, midazolam oral, triazolam, salmeterol, fluticasone, alfuzosin, drospirenone-containing COCs, rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort. Recommends Liverpool COVID interactions database (covid19-druginteractions.org) and alternative COVID therapy where contraindicated. Reads context.medications, context.creatinineUmolL, context.hepaticChildPugh — never patient identity.

references.label: Liverpool COVID-19 Interactions database — University of Liverpool

title: Sacubitril-valsartan + ACE inhibitor — contraindicated (angioedema)
description: Blocks concomitant sacubitril-valsartan and ACE inhibitor prescribing — markedly raises angioedema risk. Requires at least 36 hours' ACEi washout before initiating sacubitril-valsartan. Also blocks if patient has prior history of angioedema with ACEi or ARB. Reads context.medications, context.angiooedemaHistory — never patient identity.

title: Linezolid + serotonergic agent — serotonin syndrome
description: Fires when linezolid (weak MAOI) is prescribed alongside SSRI, SNRI, TCA, MAOI, tramadol, fentanyl, triptan, methylene blue, pethidine, or St John's wort. Recommends stopping the serotonergic agent (2 weeks washout for most, 5 weeks for fluoxetine) BEFORE linezolid, or selecting alternative antibiotic. Includes monitoring guidance if combination unavoidable. Reads context.medications — never patient identity.

references.label: FDA Drug Safety Communication on linezolid + serotonergics 2011

title: WHO HEARTS — stepwise BP-lowering protocol prompt
description: Fires for adults with confirmed hypertension whose BP remains above target on the current step. Suggests the next step: lifestyle + monotherapy → dual (ACEi/ARB + CCB) → triple (add thiazide-like diuretic) → quadruple (add spironolactone). Includes individual target (140/90 default; 130/80 in diabetes/CKD/post-stroke). Reads context.ageYears, context.systolicMmHg, context.diastolicMmHg, context.currentAntihypertensives, context.diabetes, context.ckd, context.postStroke, context.potassium, context.egfr — never patient identity.

references.label: WHO 2021 guideline on the pharmacological treatment of hypertension in adults
WHO HEARTS technical package — Evidence-based protocols module

title: Major burn — Parkland fluid resuscitation calculator
description: Fires for patient with adult burn ≥ 20% TBSA (or paeds ≥ 10%). Calculates Parkland formula (4 mL × kg × %TBSA) with half over first 8 h and remainder over next 16 h, titrated to urine output 0.5 mL/kg/h adult / 1 mL/kg/h paediatric. Includes burns-centre referral criteria, escharotomy considerations, inhalation-injury triage. Reads context.tbsaPercent, context.weightKg, context.ageYears, context.timeOfBurnHoursAgo — never patient identity.

references.label: American Burn Association ABLS provider manual
WHO Burn prevention and emergency care guidelines

codings.display: Burns classified by extent of body surface involved

title: CKD with albuminuria — ACE inhibitor / ARB recommended
description: Fires when patient has eGFR < 60 OR urine ACR ≥ 30 mg/g (≥ 3 mg/mmol) AND not currently on ACE inhibitor or ARB. Recommends initiation of ACEi or ARB (with K+ ≤ 5.0 and stable eGFR) and SGLT2 inhibitor co-prescription per KDIGO 2024 (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) for additional cardio-renal protection. Reads context.egfr, context.urineACR, context.medications, context.potassium — never patient identity.

references.label: ADA Standards of Care — Chronic kidney disease in diabetes

title: Surviving Sepsis Hour-1 bundle
description: Fires when patient meets sepsis screening criteria (qSOFA ≥ 2 OR suspected infection + organ dysfunction). Reminds: lactate, blood cultures BEFORE antibiotics (don't delay > 45 min), broad-spectrum antibiotic, 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension or lactate ≥ 4, vasopressor (noradrenaline) for MAP < 65. Reads context.qsofa, context.suspectedInfection, context.lactate, context.systolicMmHg, context.recentAntibiotic — never patient identity.

title: Severe hyperkalaemia — calcium first, then shift, then remove
description: Fires when serum K+ ≥ 6.5 OR ≥ 6.0 with ECG changes. Recommends calcium gluconate IV (cardiac protection), insulin-dextrose + nebulised salbutamol (shift), potassium binder + furosemide + haemodialysis assessment (remove). Stops contributing drugs. Reads context.potassium, context.ecgChanges, context.creatinine, context.medications — never patient identity.

references.label: UK Renal Association — Treatment of acute hyperkalaemia in adults (2020)

title: Hyponatraemia correction rate + osmotic demyelination prevention
description: Fires for serum Na+ < 130. Severe symptomatic (Na+ < 125 + seizure/coma): hypertonic saline 3% 150 mL IV with 5 mmol/L target rise acutely. Calculates total 24 h correction max (10 mmol/L; 8 if high ODS risk) and warns if exceeding. Detects over-correction and recommends DDAVP / dextrose to re-lower. Reads context.serumSodium, context.symptoms, context.hypokalaemia, context.alcohol, context.malnutrition, context.liverDisease — never patient identity.

title: Adrenal crisis recognition + stress-dose steroid
description: Fires for shock unresponsive to fluids in patient with known adrenal insufficiency / chronic glucocorticoid use, OR with hyponatraemia + hyperkalaemia + hypoglycaemia. Recommends IMMEDIATE hydrocortisone 100 mg IV bolus then 200 mg/24 h, with saline + dextrose. Reads context.knownAdrenalInsufficiency, context.chronicSteroid, context.sodium, context.potassium, context.glucose, context.systolicMmHg — never patient identity.

title: Acute variceal haemorrhage care bundle
description: Fires for upper GI bleed in cirrhosis. Recommends: airway protection, restrictive transfusion (Hb 70–80), terlipressin / octreotide, IV ceftriaxone prophylaxis 1 g daily, urgent endoscopy < 12 h, balloon tamponade if uncontrolled, TIPS pathway. Reads context.cirrhosis, context.haematemesis, context.melaena, context.hb — never patient identity.

title: Massive PE — systemic thrombolysis decision support
description: Fires for high-risk PE (haemodynamic instability + confirmed PE) without absolute bleeding contraindications. Recommends alteplase 100 mg over 2 h (or 50 mg over 1–2 h higher bleed risk) + UFH post-lysis. Lists alternatives (catheter-directed lysis, surgical embolectomy) for contraindications. Reads context.peDiagnosis, context.systolicMmHg, context.bleedingContraindication — never patient identity.

title: Paracetamol overdose — nomogram + NAC initiation
description: Fires for any paracetamol ingestion. Calculates dose / kg, time since ingestion. Recommends NAC if: level above Rumack-Matthew 100 mg/L line at 4–24 h post-acute single ingestion; OR staggered ingestion > 75 mg/kg; OR late presentation (> 8 h) empirically. Provides 21-h or SNAP 12-h regimen calculator. Reads context.paracetamolDose, context.weightKg, context.timeOfIngestionHours, context.serumParacetamolLevel, context.alt, context.inr — never patient identity.

references.label: MHRA / UK Toxbase paracetamol overdose protocol

title: Opioid overdose — titrated naloxone + observation
description: Fires for opioid-overdose presentation (reduced consciousness + miosis + RR < 12). Recommends bag-mask ventilation, titrated IV naloxone starting 40–100 microgram (low to avoid precipitated withdrawal), repeat every 2–3 min to ventilation. Naloxone infusion for long-acting opioid. Observation ≥ 4–6 h post-last-dose. Refer to opioid agonist therapy + take-home naloxone. Reads context.respiratoryRate, context.gcs, context.pupilSize, context.suspectedOpioid — never patient identity.

references.label: WHO Community management of opioid overdose 2014

title: Lithium toxicity — recognition + dialysis criteria
description: Fires for lithium-treated patient with new tremor, ataxia, confusion, GI symptoms, or serum lithium > 1.5 mmol/L. EXTRIP haemodialysis criteria: lithium > 4.0 mmol/L; 2.5–4.0 with severe symptoms or renal failure; chronic toxicity with neurological symptoms. Stop lithium + interacting drugs (NSAID, ACEi, thiazide, diuretic). IV 0.9% NaCl rehydration. Reads context.lithiumLevel, context.creatinine, context.symptoms, context.medications — never patient identity.

title: Beta-blocker / calcium channel blocker overdose — high-dose insulin euglycaemia
description: Fires for suspected β-blocker or CCB overdose with hypotension / bradycardia / cardiogenic shock. Recommends: atropine + fluid first, then IV calcium (CCB), glucagon (β-blocker), high-dose insulin euglycaemia (HIE) 1 unit/kg bolus then 0.5–10 units/kg/h with dextrose, lipid emulsion for refractory, VA-ECMO. Reads context.suspectedToxin, context.heartRate, context.systolicMmHg, context.glucose, context.medications — never patient identity.

references.label: AACT / ACMT consensus on BB / CCB overdose

title: Methanol / ethylene glycol poisoning — fomepizole + dialysis criteria
description: Fires for HAGMA + raised osmolal gap, especially with visual changes (methanol) or AKI/calcium oxalate crystals (ethylene glycol). Recommends fomepizole 15 mg/kg IV loading then 10 mg/kg every 12 h (alternative IV ethanol). Haemodialysis for severe acidosis, visual symptoms, AKI, or level > 50 mg/dL. Adjuncts: folinic acid for methanol; pyridoxine + thiamine for ethylene glycol. Reads context.anionGap, context.osmolalGap, context.visualSymptoms, context.creatinine, context.suspectedIngestion — never patient identity.

references.label: AACT fomepizole position; EXTRIP toxic-alcohol recommendations

title: Myasthenic crisis recognition + treatment pathway
description: Fires for myasthenia gravis with FVC < 20 mL/kg or single-breath count < 25 or bulbar symptoms. Recommends elective intubation, plasma exchange OR IVIG, stop offending drugs (aminoglycoside, fluoroquinolone, β-blocker, magnesium, telithromycin), cautious steroid initiation (avoid worsening), thymectomy if thymoma. Reads context.knownMyasthenia, context.fvc, context.singleBreathCount, context.bulbarSymptoms, context.medications — never patient identity.

references.label: International Consensus Guidance for MG (Sanders et al. Neurology 2020)

title: Suspected viral encephalitis — empirical aciclovir + LP within 6 h
description: Fires for fever + new altered mental state / personality / focal seizure / new focal neurology. Recommends MRI (CT if not available), urgent LP unless contraindicated, EMPIRICAL IV aciclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 h immediately + ceftriaxone (+ amoxicillin if ≥ 50/immunocompromised). Continue 14–21 days for HSV-positive PCR. Reads context.fever, context.alteredConsciousness, context.seizureNewOnset, context.focalNeurology — never patient identity.

title: Thyroid storm — Burch-Wartofsky + bundled therapy
description: Fires for severe thyrotoxicosis with hyperpyrexia / arrhythmia / cardiac failure / altered consciousness. Calculates Burch-Wartofsky score; recommends bundled therapy: PTU 500–1000 mg load then 200 mg every 4 h, Lugol's iodine 1 h after thionamide, propranolol or esmolol, hydrocortisone 100 mg every 6 h, supportive cooling. Treat precipitant. Reads context.knownHyperthyroidism, context.temperature, context.heartRate, context.atrialFibrillation, context.gcs — never patient identity.

title: TOF hypercyanotic spell management
description: Fires for known TOF or undiagnosed cyanotic CHD with acute SpO2 fall + hyperpnoea. Recommends knee-chest position, calm + O2, morphine, fluid bolus, phenylephrine, propranolol. WARNS against inotropes that worsen RVOT obstruction. Reads context.knownTof, context.suspectedCyanoticCHD, context.spO2, context.heartRate — never patient identity.

references.label: AHA Guidelines for CHD; Park's Pediatric Cardiology

title: Suspected ductal-dependent CHD — start prostaglandin
description: Fires for newborn (≤ 28 days) presenting with cyanosis OR shock + weak femoral pulses OR pre/post-ductal SpO2 differential > 3%. Recommends IV alprostadil (PGE1) 0.05 microgram/kg/min IMMEDIATELY pending echo; prepare for intubation (apnoea risk); avoid hyperoxia in ductal-dependent systemic lesion. Reads context.ageDays, context.spO2PreDuctal, context.spO2PostDuctal, context.femoralPulse, context.shock — never patient identity.

title: Paediatric SVT — vagal then adenosine pathway
description: Fires for narrow-complex tachycardia: infant > 220, child > 180, adolescent > 150. Recommends vagal manoeuvres first; adenosine 0.1 mg/kg rapid IV (escalate 0.2; max 12 mg single dose); synchronised cardioversion 0.5–1 J/kg if unstable. WARNS against verapamil in infants. Reads context.ageYears, context.heartRate, context.systolicMmHg, context.gcs — never patient identity.

title: Severe bronchiolitis — supportive-only pathway
description: Fires for infant < 1 year with bronchiolitis + SpO2 < 92% / apnoea / severe distress / feeding < 50%. Recommends O2 / HFNC / NIV, NG or IV feeds, minimal handling. WARNS against bronchodilator, corticosteroid, antibiotic, hypertonic saline routinely. Reads context.ageMonths, context.spO2, context.respiratoryRate, context.feedingTolerance, context.apnoea — never patient identity.

title: Severe croup — dexamethasone + nebulised adrenaline
description: Fires for moderate-severe croup (stridor at rest, recession). Recommends dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg PO (or 0.6 mg/kg if severe / cannot tolerate oral), nebulised adrenaline 5 mg for stridor at rest, observe ≥ 2–4 h post-adrenaline. WARNS against tongue depressor examination if epiglottitis possible. Reads context.ageYears, context.westleyScore, context.spO2, context.drooling, context.toxicAppearance — never patient identity.

title: Kawasaki disease — IVIG + aspirin + coronary echo
description: Fires for child with fever ≥ 5 days + Kawasaki criteria OR coronary aneurysm on echo. Recommends IVIG 2 g/kg single dose + high-dose aspirin (30–50 mg/kg/day) until afebrile 48 h then 3–5 mg/kg/day × 6–8 weeks. Adjunctive steroids for high-risk (< 1 year, coronary dilation, KDSS). Echo at diagnosis + 1–2 weeks + 4–6 weeks. Reads context.ageYears, context.feverDays, context.kawasakiCriteria, context.coronaryDilation — never patient identity.

references.label: AHA Scientific Statement: KD diagnosis + management 2017

title: Severe hypothermia — ECMO rewarming criteria
description: Fires for core temperature < 28°C with cardiac instability / arrest. Recommends gentle handling; CPR if no signs of life; minimal drug administration < 30°C; active rewarming (ECMO preferred for unstable; warmed IV, body cavity lavage second-line). DO NOT PRONOUNCE DEAD until warm and dead (core > 32°C). K+ > 12 adult / > 20 child suggests irreversibility. Reads context.coreTemperature, context.cardiacRhythm, context.potassium — never patient identity.

title: Severe heat stroke — rapid cooling protocol
description: Fires for core temperature > 40°C with CNS dysfunction. Recommends cold-water immersion (preferred for exertional), evaporative + ice packs (classical / unstable); IV fluid resuscitation; STOP cooling at 38.5–39°C. WARNS against paracetamol / NSAID / dantrolene. Reads context.coreTemperature, context.gcs, context.seizure, context.creatineKinase — never patient identity.

references.label: Korey Stringer Institute; Wilderness Medical Society

title: Ruptured AAA — permissive hypotension + EVAR-first
description: Fires for sudden severe abdominal/back pain + hypotension + (pulsatile mass OR known AAA OR USS evidence). Recommends permissive hypotension SBP 70–90 / palpable radial; massive transfusion 1:1:1; activate vascular team for EVAR (preferred) or open repair. Reads context.suspectedRaaa, context.knownAaa, context.systolicMmHg — never patient identity.

title: Acute limb ischaemia — heparin + Rutherford classification
description: Fires for 6 Ps (pain, pallor, pulselessness, paraesthesia, paralysis, perishing cold). Classifies Rutherford I/IIa/IIb/III. Recommends immediate IV heparin (80 units/kg bolus); urgent vascular consult; surgical embolectomy / catheter-directed thrombolysis for IIa-IIb. Primary amputation for III. Reads context.painOnset, context.pulses, context.sensation, context.motor — never patient identity.

title: Severe dengue — phase-based fluid management
description: Fires for dengue patient with warning signs OR severe plasma leak / shock / bleeding. Recommends Group A/B/C WHO classification + matched fluid regimen (5–7 mL/kg/h reducing; aggressive bolus for shock; colloid if refractory). WARNS against prophylactic platelet transfusion + aspirin/NSAID. Recovery phase: reduce fluids. Reads context.dengueDayOfIllness, context.hct, context.platelet, context.warningSign, context.shock — never patient identity.

title: Cerebral malaria — IV artesunate + supportive care
description: Fires for confirmed P. falciparum parasitaemia with GCS < 11 / coma / repeated seizures. Recommends IV artesunate 2.4 mg/kg at 0, 12, 24 h then daily; empirical IV ceftriaxone (Salmonella cover); RESTRICTIVE fluid resuscitation (FEAST); glucose monitoring; transfusion if Hb < 5 g/dL. Reads context.parasitaemiaConfirmed, context.gcs, context.seizureNew, context.hb, context.glucose — never patient identity.

title: Acute rheumatic fever — Jones criteria + secondary prophylaxis
description: Fires for child with possible ARF features (carditis, arthritis, chorea, erythema marginatum, nodules + minor criteria). Recommends IM benzathine penicillin G; aspirin / NSAID for arthritis; steroid for severe carditis; echocardiography. SECONDARY PROPHYLAXIS lifelong / extended per carditis status. Reads context.ageYears, context.feverDuration, context.jonesMajor, context.jonesMinor, context.asoTitre, context.echoFindings — never patient identity.

title: HUS — supportive care; AVOID antibiotics in STEC
description: Fires for child with diarrhoea (often bloody) + microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia + thrombocytopenia + AKI. Recommends supportive care, careful fluid balance, RRT criteria, packed cells for severe anaemia. WARNS against antibiotics for STEC enteritis (may worsen HUS) + against prophylactic platelet transfusion. Refer for eculizumab assessment if atypical / refractory. Reads context.ageYears, context.diarrhoeaBloody, context.hb, context.platelet, context.creatinine, context.urineOutput — never patient identity.

title: Botulism — antitoxin + public-health notification
description: Fires for symmetric descending flaccid paralysis (cranial nerves first) without sensory deficit. Recommends IMMEDIATE public-health notification, equine heptavalent antitoxin (adult/child > 1 year) or BabyBIG (infant). Respiratory monitoring + elective intubation for FVC < 30%. WARNS against aminoglycoside antibiotics. Reads context.cranialNerveWeakness, context.descendingParalysis, context.fvc, context.ageMonths — never patient identity.

title: MIS-C — IVIG + steroids combination therapy
description: Fires for child / adolescent with fever ≥ 3 days + raised inflammatory markers + multi-organ involvement (≥ 2 systems) + recent SARS-CoV-2 exposure. Recommends IVIG 2 g/kg + methylprednisolone 1–2 mg/kg/day combined therapy (superior to IVIG alone). Aspirin 3–5 mg/kg/day for coronary protection. Anakinra / infliximab for refractory. Reads context.ageYears, context.feverDays, context.crp, context.ferritin, context.troponin, context.echoFindings, context.covidExposure — never patient identity.

references.label: WHO MIS-C scientific brief; ACR clinical guidance

title: Maternal sepsis — Hour-1 bundle with pregnancy-compatible antibiotics
description: Fires for pregnant / postpartum woman (≤ 42 days) with sepsis criteria. Recommends Hour-1 bundle modified: cultures + lactate + IV piperacillin-tazobactam + clindamycin (covers GAS toxin + anaerobes) ± gentamicin; expedite delivery for chorioamnionitis / septic abortion / retained products; IVIG for streptococcal toxic shock. Reads context.pregnant, context.daysPostpartum, context.suspectedChorioamnionitis, context.lactate — never patient identity.

title: Acute cholangitis — Tokyo Grade + biliary drainage timing
description: Fires for Charcot triad (RUQ pain + fever + jaundice) or biliary obstruction with sepsis. Calculates Tokyo grade I/II/III. Recommends IV antibiotic (pip-tazo or ceftriaxone+metronidazole), urgent ERCP drainage timing: Grade I within 48 h, Grade II within 24 h, Grade III within 12 h after stabilisation. Reads context.fever, context.bilirubin, context.alp, context.lactate, context.organDysfunction — never patient identity.

title: Perforated viscus — antibiotic + urgent surgery
description: Fires for free intraperitoneal air on imaging with peritonitic abdomen. Recommends: NG decompression, IV pip-tazo + metronidazole, resuscitation, theatre within 6 h. Reads context.freeAirOnImaging, context.peritonism, context.lactate, context.systolicMmHg — never patient identity.

title: Sigmoid volvulus — endoscopic decompression vs surgery
